decisions.quote: In this replication study, we examined the effect of educators’ participation in a practice-based professional learning series for designing, implementing, and evaluating Functional Assessment-based Interventions (FABI; Umbreit, Liaupsin, Ferro, & Lane, 2007) on their actual knowledge and perceived knowledge, confidence, and usefulness of concepts taught. Participants completed the Knowledge, Confidence, and Use Survey prior to and at the conclusion of the six-part learning series. Consistent with earlier inquiry, results indicated participants demonstrated statistically significant improvements in the constructs measured.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. The abstract-only source states that this replication study examined educators' participation in a six-part FABI professional learning series using the Knowledge, Confidence, and Use Survey and found statistically significant improvements '[c]onsistent with earlier inquiry.' While Umbreit et al. (2007) is cited for the FABI intervention framework itself, the abstract does not name the authors, year, or title of the replicated 'earlier inquiry,' and no reference list is present in the supplied source text. Shipped row 100 is Lane, Oakes, Powers, Diebold, Germer, Common, and Brunsting (2015), 'Improving Teachers’ Knowledge of Functional Assessment-based Interventions: Outcomes of a Professional Development Series' (Education and Treatment of Children, 38(1), 93-120, DOI 10.1353/etc.2015.0001). The unresolved question is whether the unnamed 'earlier inquiry' in the abstract is shipped row 100 or another prior study of the FABI professional learning series.
